questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Content Projection”?
options: Content Projection means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Content Projection removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Content Projection should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Content Projection helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Content Projection helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Content Projection is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “The <ng-content> element” in this lesson?
options: Assume “The <ng-content> element” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “The <ng-content> element” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “The <ng-content> element” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “The <ng-content> element” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “The <ng-content> element” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “The <ng-content> element” under Content Projection. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Content Projection”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
